title: Garlic-Sesame Galbisal
shortDescription: Boneless beef rib meat lightly seasoned with garlic, soy, toasted sesame, scallions, salt, and pepper for fast high-heat grilling.
culturalContext: Galbisal refers to boneless meat from around or between the ribs and is commonly treated as a premium grilling cut. It may be served unseasoned or lightly seasoned; this garlic-sesame version is one defined preparation, not a universal standard.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

totalTime.display: 1 hour 3 minutes, including seasoning and rest

equipment: Nonreactive mixing bowl or food-safe zip bag
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill

ingredients.item: boneless beef rib meat or well-marbled boneless short-rib meat
ingredients.preparation: trimmed and cut into 4 cm / 1 1/2-inch pieces

marinadeOrSeasoning.meatWeightCovered: 900 g / 2 lb boneless beef rib meat
mixOrder: Whisk soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, and pepper.
Fold in garlic, scallions, and crushed sesame seeds.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Nonreactive bowl or food-safe zip bag on a rimmed tray
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 4 hours; the small pieces can become overly salty and garlic-dominant.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: This batch is for raw beef only; make a separate clean batch if extra sauce is wanted.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard seasoning liquid remaining after raw-beef contact; do not spoon it onto cooked meat.
substitutions: Boneless short-rib meat may substitute for labeled galbisal; marbling and chew will vary.
Certified gluten-free tamari may replace soy sauce after label review.
allergenNotes: Regular soy sauce usually contains wheat.

instructions.heading: Cut the beef evenly
instructions.action: Trim only hard exterior fat or silverskin and cut the chilled meat into 4 cm / 1 1/2-inch pieces of even thickness.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Pieces are evenly sized with visible marbling and no thick bands of tough silverskin.
instructions.safetyNote: Sanitize the knife, board, and counter after raw-beef preparation.

instructions.heading: Mix the seasoning
instructions.action: Whisk soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, and pepper; fold in garlic, scallions, and crushed sesame seeds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Garlic and scallions are evenly suspended in a thin glossy seasoning.
instructions.safetyNote: Make any serving sauce as a separate batch before raw beef is added.

instructions.heading: Season briefly under refrigeration
instructions.action: Massage seasoning into the beef, cover, and refrigerate 20 to 30 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Every piece is lightly coated; no large pool of sauce remains.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not leave raw seasoned beef at room temperature or hold it longer than 4 hours.

instructions.heading: Preheat the cooking surface
instructions.action: Preheat a clean approved grill to medium-high and oil lightly. Arrange a clean cooked-food platter and clean utensils.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: A piece of beef produces an immediate strong sizzle.
instructions.safetyNote: For indoor use, follow the manufacturer’s ventilation and clearance instructions for an approved electric appliance.

instructions.heading: Grill in a single layer
instructions.action: Grill pieces without crowding, turning to brown multiple sides, about 6 to 9 minutes depending on thickness.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Surfaces are deeply browned; the center of the thickest piece reaches the target temperature.
instructions.safetyNote: Use the thermometer in the center of the thickest piece and transfer with clean utensils.

instructions.heading: Rest before serving
instructions.action: Move the beef to the clean platter and rest at least 3 minutes before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Juices settle and the pieces remain springy and moist.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not add leftover raw-contact seasoning.

grillSetup: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill to medium-high, about 400–450°F / 204–232°C. Follow the appliance manual for clearance and ventilation; never use charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical portion, followed by a 3-minute rest
visualDonenessCues: Multiple sides are browned while the interior remains moist.
The center of the thickest piece reaches 145°F / 63°C before a 3-minute rest.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep raw beef and its marinade separate from ready-to-eat foods; wash hands and sanitize contacted surfaces.
Use separate raw and cooked plates and utensils, or wash and sanitize them fully before reuse.
Measure the thickest practical portion with a calibrated food thermometer; grill marks and time alone do not establish doneness.
For whole-cut beef, reach 145°F / 63°C and rest for at least 3 minutes before serving.
Use only an outdoor grill or an electric tabletop appliance explicitly approved by its manufacturer for indoor use; follow ventilation and clearance instructions.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Check every packaged-ingredient label and prevent cross-contact; substitutions do not guarantee an allergen-free result.

substitutions: Boneless short-rib meat is the closest practical substitute; chuck or lean stew meat will not cook the same way.
Certified gluten-free tamari changes only the soy sauce component; all labels and cross-contact still require review.
ingredientSourcing: Ask a Korean butcher for galbisal or boneless rib meat intended for grilling.
Choose evenly marbled pieces rather than lean stew cubes.
makeAhead: Cut the beef and mix the seasoning separately up to 1 day ahead. Combine only 20 to 30 minutes before grilling; do not season longer than 4 hours.
storage: Refrigerate cooked beef within 2 hours in a shallow airtight container at 40°F / 4°C or below; use within 3 days.
reheating: Reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Reheat only the portion needed and avoid prolonged cooking that toughens thin beef.
leftovers: Reheat to 165°F / 74°C and slice into rice bowls or wraps; avoid repeated reheating.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice, fresh ssam greens, and a light salad.
Place additional salt-sesame dip on the table only if prepared separately with reviewed allergen labeling.

faq.question: What cut can replace galbisal?
faq.answer: Well-marbled boneless short-rib meat is the closest practical substitute. Lean stew meat is likely to be tougher with this fast grilling method.

faq.question: Why is the seasoning time short?
faq.answer: Small beef pieces absorb salt and garlic quickly; a brief refrigerated rest seasons the surface without turning the dish excessively salty.
